about: The contract of the translation providers (issue #277).

Each case gives what is asked of a provider (operation, access, translation) and what the provider answers (answers: replies in order per method and URL; the last reply repeats; {"error": "connect"} is a connection that fails).

`python` is what the Python clients of src-python/models/translation/ sent and returned for the case, recorded by src-python/test/test_translation_contract.py (VRCT_TRANSLATION_CONTRACT_WRITE=1 records again).

native/translation/tests/contract.rs runs every case against the Rust providers and compares with `python`, after the differences the case names. `rust` replaces `python` where the core behaves differently on purpose; `expect` is the record of a provider Python never had, written from the provider's documentation.
Requests are compared by method, URL, headers other than transport noise, JSON body and timeouts. Outcomes: check {accepted, models}, models {models}, translate {text} or {failed: true}.

A reply may carry headers (retry-after, x-should-retry). `retry_pause` is the range of seconds the SDK waits before its retry (its rule has a random part); both tests check the time between the first two requests against it.

local-openai-compatible.why: An OpenAI-compatible endpoint on this PC or the LAN gets the wait of LM Studio and no retry (read 120 seconds, one try), since it is a server the user runs. Python gave it the cloud's 30 seconds and one retry.
local-openai-compatible.decided: docs/voice-stack/core-integration.md, 決まったこと, 翻訳のプロバイダ (1)

cases.note: A key ending in :fx goes to the free API; the check translates one space to EN-US.
A refused key is not tried again.
The check has no retry.
Codes as the DeepL table gives them; the request carries them upper-cased.
